title: Combined Entitlement Ceiling - Education Benefits Across Chapters
content:
A beneficiary of Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education) who holds two or more chapters can use no more than 48 months of entitlement in total across all of them, even though each chapter grants its own 36 months.

**Measuring what has been used.** The months used across all chapters are measured over the beneficiary's lifetime: for every education benefit the beneficiary holds, the entitlement granted less the entitlement remaining, those days added together across all the benefits and divided by 30 to give months. Chapter 35 entitlement used as a dependent counts toward the ceiling together with the chapters earned through the beneficiary's own service.

**The charge that reaches the ceiling.** When the next charge would cross the combined ceiling, only the days up to the ceiling are charged and paid; the benefit that still shows remaining days is then treated as having none.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Total used after the next charge stays at or below 48 months | The charge is made in full |
| The next charge would take the total above 48 months | Only the days up to 48 months are charged and paid; the benefit with days remaining is treated as having none |

**Worked illustration (hypothetical figures).** A beneficiary has used 900 days of Chapter 35 as a child and 450 days of the Post-9/11 GI Bill: 1350 days, or 45 months. The ceiling of 48 months is 1440 days. A term whose charge would be 120 days would take the total to 1470 days, above the ceiling, so only 90 days are charged and paid; the Post-9/11 benefit is then treated as having no days left, whatever balance it shows.
